sections.h2: China and Russia hold most of the $228.5bn rupee residual each year

chart.title: China and Russia make up most of the residual rupee claim
chart.sub: Residual trade (imports not covered by exports), US$ billion, FY2025-26.
chart.source: Ministry of Commerce & Industry, TradeStat; author's calculation.

sections.means: The residual is the rupee balance a partner must hold after both legs net out, and China alone accounts for $112.1bn of it.
sections.todo: Treat the China and Russia residuals as vendor financing to be negotiated on price, not assumed as settlement.

sections.h2: Export coverage of BRICS imports fell from 44% to 29.8% in a decade

chart.title: The share of BRICS imports that exports cover has shrunk for a decade
chart.sub: Exports to BRICS as a share of imports from BRICS, %.
chart.source: Ministry of Commerce & Industry, TradeStat; author's calculation.

sections.means: Because exports cover a smaller share of imports each year, the part of BRICS trade that can be settled in rupees without building claims is shrinking.
sections.todo: Focus rupee settlement on the partners where the table shows trade closest to balance, not on China or Russia.

sections.h2: Only netting is sustainable; full settlement needs $228.5bn of rupee claims a year

chart.title: Netting alone would settle $93.4bn a year, against $17.8bn today
chart.sub: Gross BRICS import demand removed from the dollar, US$ billion a year.
chart.source: Author's scenario model on Ministry of Commerce TradeStat data, FY2025-26.

sections.means: Netting is sustainable, while full BRICS settlement creates rupee claims that partners must absorb every year.
sections.todo: Pursue S2 netting and payment-friction fixes, and do not plan on S3 unless partners are willing to hold rupees.
